sections.html: Corydoras sarareensis Dinkelmeyer, 1995. Common names: C023, Sarare Cory. Type locality: Rio Sararé, right side branch of Rio Guaporé, Mato Grosso State, Brazil. Size: 65 mm SL. Corydoras are identified by their twin rows of armour plates along the flanks and by having fewer than 10 dorsal fin rays. They are most commonly confused with the other genera in the sub-family, namely Brochis, Scleromystax and Aspidoras.
South America: Guaporé River basin in Brazil. Amazon, Middle Amazon (Solimoes), Madeira, Mamoré, Guaporé (Iténez). IUCN Red List category: Least Concern (last assessed 2018).

Ideally substrate should be sand, but rounded gravel is an imperfect alternative. Avoid keeping over rough edged (chipped) gravel, as this will increase the risk of damage to the fish's barbels when it tries to dig. Substrate should be bordered with driftwood and aquatic plants, leaving an open area for them to search for food and swim. The shade provided by overhanging rock work, arching bogwood, tall or floating plants is all that is required to settle these fish.

Will readily accept all prepared foods that reach the bottom of the aquarium such as tablets, granules and larger flakes. Live (or frozen) foods such as bloodworm, white worm, grindal worm (Enchytraeus), Daphnia and Tubifex are readily accepted and good for conditioning groups of fish for spawning.
Females grow larger and are more full-bodied, which is best observed from above the fish. Males will typically have more pointed rather than rounded fin tips as they mature.
